content:
According to 9to5Mac's website traffic analysis, Apple is testing the iOS 27.0.1 version. iPhone users are expected to receive this update within the next few days, which is anticipated to focus on bug fixes and performance improvements.

iOS 27.0.1 is coming soon

iOS 27.0.1 started appearing in 9to5Mac's traffic analysis a few days ago. MacRumors has also reported the same situation.

9to5Mac this morning cited Apple as saying that a software update will be released early next week to fix an issue where some iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max devices restart after a failed Face ID recognition.

We reported this issue a few days ago, explaining that this situation occurs when you try to use Face ID to open apps like 'Passwords'. If Face ID fails, your iPhone may suddenly restart.

My iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max has never experienced this issue, but it's clear that quite a few users have been affected. The good news is that this bug can be fixed through software, rather than being a hardware malfunction.

iOS 27.0.1 will very likely address the aforementioned issue, but it has not yet been confirmed. The update may also include other bug fixes affecting iOS 27 and the new iPhone 18 Pro hardware.

Have you encountered any issues since upgrading to iOS 27? Or are there any iPhone 18 Pro-exclusive problems? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
